# jpegoptim / libjpeg_compression_fuzzer

jpegoptim's own fuzz target `libjpeg_compression_fuzzer` ([source](source/fuzz_compression.c), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over jpegoptim (tjko/jpegoptim at 14a3155a).

Writes the input to a /dev/shm mkstemp file and calls jpegoptim's whole CLI pipeline optimize() on it (decode, recompress at target size -75%, keep if smaller), logging to /dev/null. optimize()'s result and the output file are never inspected. It returns -1 (reject from corpus, not a crash) if lstat, fopen or fwrite fail.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against jpegoptim at commit 14a3155a.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
The harness makes no check of its own beyond not crashing, so a statement about it says only that the code it calls never crashes, hangs or trips a sanitizer.

Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch jpegoptim` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libturbojpeg.a` (a library from the build image)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libturbojpeg.a` (a library from the build image)
